did_you_know.text: Did you know? Zedekiah was made king of Judah in place of Coniah (Jehoiachin) after Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, appointed him king over the land of Judah.
Did you know? Although Zedekiah, his officials, and the people of the land heard the words of the Lord spoken through Jeremiah, they did not obey them.
Did you know? Zedekiah sent Jehucal son of Shelemiah and Zephaniah the priest to Jeremiah and asked him to pray to the Lord on their behalf.
Did you know? When Pharaoh’s army left Egypt, the Chaldeans besieging Jerusalem heard about it and withdrew from the city for a time.
Did you know? Jeremiah warned the people of Jerusalem not to be misled into hoping that the Chaldeans had withdrawn for good; he said they would return and fight against the city.

Did you know? According to the word of the Lord, even if the people of Jerusalem managed to defeat the entire Chaldean army, leaving only wounded men, those men would still rise from their tents and burn the city.
Did you know? While the Chaldeans had withdrawn from Jerusalem, Jeremiah left the city to go to the land of Benjamin and receive his share there among the people.
Did you know? Jeremiah was arrested at the Benjamin Gate after Jeraiah son of Shelemiah accused him of defecting to the Chaldeans, meaning that he was joining them or going over to their side.
Did you know? Zedekiah secretly asked Jeremiah whether there was a word from the Lord, and Jeremiah answered him that the king would be handed over to the king of Babylon.
Did you know? At Jeremiah’s request, Zedekiah ordered that he be kept in the courtyard of the guard and given a loaf of bread each day, until all the bread in the city was gone.
